replies.body: @laurit @jaydeluca If we only focus on database scenarios such as Jedis and Lettuce, we will have to implement targeted handling for these two libraries. However, there are also non-database use cases. For instance, Thrift relies on commons-pool2 object pools to manage socket connections, where commons-pool2 is used as a standalone dependency instead of being built into Thrift. Such scenarios would not be covered under the database-only approach. Which of the two solutions do you recommend? Should we only instrument database-related components like Jedis and Lettuce, or instrument the entire commons-pool2 module with a feature toggle to enable or disable the capability?

If you go for a generic instrumentation for commons pool then probably the library instrumentation will work well but in agent instrumentation it might be difficult to create names identifying the pools when jmx is disabled. Also with just commons pool instrumentation you can't use the db connection pool semconv, a separate semconv for generic object pools might be needed.

@laurit From my understanding of establishing a dedicated observability semantic convention exclusively for generic object pools, are you suggesting that we should not define a set of apache-commons-pool-specific observability semantics within ObjectPoolMetrics? Instead, we ought to define a universal set of observability semantics for object pools similar to DbConnectionPoolMetrics, so that they can be reused by other object pool implementations in the future?

@laurit Regarding your point that it would be difficult to create unique names for identifying individual object pools if JMX is disabled: our current implementation already accounts for this scenario. If the value retrieved via objectName.getKeyProperty("name") is null, we will fall back to the jmxNamePrefix configured in BaseObjectPoolConfig.

>  From my understanding of establishing a dedicated observability semantic convention exclusively for generic object pools, are you suggesting that we should not define a set of apache-commons-pool-specific observability semantics within ObjectPoolMetrics? Instead, we ought to define a universal set of observability semantics for object pools similar to DbConnectionPoolMetrics, so that they can be reused by other object pool implementations in the future?

Our current convention is that by default we only emit telemetry that has semantic conventions. Having semantic conventions isn't required, but would be nice. Of course defining the semantic conventions is a ton of work and might not lead anywhere.

> Regarding your point that it would be difficult to create unique names for identifying individual object pools if JMX is disabled: our current implementation already accounts for this scenario. If the value retrieved via objectName.getKeyProperty("name") is null, we will fall back to the jmxNamePrefix configured in BaseObjectPoolConfig.

With library instrumentations it will be easy, we can just ask the user to provide a name. With agent the problem is that if the user has 5 pools and we use the same name for all of them then the user will probably get the warning that the same metric was reported multiple times in one collection cycle. If we add a suffix like `-2` to the name then it still might not be possible for the user to tell which pool it really is. I guess it isn't too bad since at least there is an option to specify the name. We probably have to push the responsibility of giving names to the pools to the user and just accept that this can't be done automatically.
For example in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/15759 the problem is that agent can't produce an identifier for created metrics. There have been asks for java executor metrics that have the same issue, how do you identify which executor the metrics are for?

> Another point I’d like to discuss is that both Jedis and Lettuce use Apache Commons Pool as their connection pool implementation. For instance, can we instrument redis.clients.jedis.util.Pool in Jedis to obtain the underlying GenericObjectPool instance, and then export connection pool metrics via DbConnectionPoolMetrics?

I wouldn't worry about this, as you have noted yourself solutions for it exist.

replies.body: @laurit This naming logic actually references the native logic of commons-pool itself: https://github.com/apache/commons-pool/blob/3c183f68d4f8ede83805c5e4ebc2c4b1de09081c/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/pool3/impl/BaseGenericObjectPool.java#L1179. When jmxEnabled is set to true, this logic is executed by default to ensure the uniqueness of the name. However, if it is set to false, metrics will still be recorded and this logic will not be executed. Therefore, a fallback mechanism was implemented, and now I am removing this logic.

This is public library API, and taking `Object` means callers can pass anything and get silence — `CommonsPoolMetrics.registerMetrics` falls through both `instanceof` branches and does nothing. `ApacheDbcpTelemetry` takes a typed `BasicDataSourceMXBean` for this reason.

Suggest two overloads here (and on `unregisterMetrics`): one for `GenericObjectPoolMXBean` and one for `GenericKeyedObjectPoolMXBean<?>`, so an unsupported pool is a compile error instead of silently missing metrics.

For keyed pools these are per-key targets/caps, but they feed `apache.commons_pool.object.idle.min` / `.max`, whose descriptions say "allowed in the pool". So the same metric means pool-wide for `GenericObjectPool` and per-key for `GenericKeyedObjectPool`, and a consumer can't tell which without knowing the pool type.

Suggest not emitting these two for keyed pools. The rest (`object.count`, `object.max`, `object.pending_requests`) are pool-wide totals in both cases, so they stay consistent.

Advising the base-class constructor registers the batch callback while the concrete pool is still half-built: `GenericObjectPool` assigns `allObjects` and `idleObjects` after `super(...)` returns, and `getNumActive()` / `getNumIdle()` read both. A metric collection landing in that window throws. If the subclass constructor then fails, the callback is also left registered for a pool that never existed.

Suggest advising the `GenericObjectPool` and `GenericKeyedObjectPool` constructors instead, so registration happens after the pool is fully initialized.

These two properties don't do anything yet. The metadata collector only runs the test tasks listed in `.github/scripts/instrumentations.sh`, and `apache-commons-pool-2.0:javaagent:test` isn't there, so the metrics metadata for this module never gets generated. Please add the module to that script - #19152 does the same thing for redisson.

Separately, this module has a `library/README.md` but no `javaagent/README.md`, so there's nowhere documenting `otel.instrumentation.apache-commons-pool.enabled`. Other new modules with a disabled-by-default toggle ship one.

[Naming] Suggest `apache_commons_pool.*` as the root namespace instead of `apache.commons_pool.*`, i.e. the module name (`apache-commons-pool`) with hyphens replaced by underscores.

That matches what we already do elsewhere (`failsafe-3.0` -> `failsafe.*`, `iceberg-1.8` -> `iceberg.*`) and it lines up with the `java.apache_commons_pool.enabled` declarative name in this PR's `metadata.yaml`.

Concretely:

| current | suggested |
| --- | --- |
| `apache.commons_pool.object.count` | `apache_commons_pool.object.count` |
| `apache.commons_pool.object.idle.min` / `.max` | `apache_commons_pool.object.idle.min` / `.max` |
| `apache.commons_pool.object.max` | `apache_commons_pool.object.max` |
| `apache.commons_pool.object.pending_requests` | `apache_commons_pool.object.pending_requests` |
| `apache.commons_pool.object.state` | `apache_commons_pool.object.state` |
| `apache.commons_pool.pool.name` | `apache_commons_pool.pool.name` |

Keeping the `pool.name` tail seems right: it parallels the `.object.*` sub-namespace and mirrors `db.client.connection.pool.name`.

Would also need updating in the two READMEs and `metadata.yaml`.

[Testing] `hasAttributesSatisfying` silently ignores unexpected attributes, so these points would still pass if the instrumentation started adding an extra attribute. Convention here is `hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly`. Same in `assertObjectCountPoolNames` above.

```suggestion
                        point ->
                            point.hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(
                                equalTo(POOL_NAME, poolName), equalTo(OBJECT_STATE, "idle")),
                        point ->
                            point.hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(
                                equalTo(POOL_NAME, poolName), equalTo(OBJECT_STATE, "used"))));
```

`GenericKeyedObjectPoolConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL` is `-1`, which commons-pool treats as unlimited. So a `GenericKeyedObjectPool` that nobody configures publishes `apache_commons_pool.object.max = -1`, and any consumer computing utilization as used / max gets a nonsense number. `maxIdle` has the same issue, since a negative value there also means unlimited.

Could we skip the observation when the value is negative, instead of recording the sentinel?

The keyed pool test sets `maxTotal(10)`, so it doesn't cover the default.
